$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.query.cli.command. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-LINT-FIX-CENSUS-UNGATED
arms.note: the zero-edit gate is dropped, so a `--fix` run that wrote nothing prints the whole per-rule accounting about it again - ~1450 bytes of stderr per write op, which is what the slice measured and removed

arms.name: M-REGION-NOTES-ALWAYS
arms.note: the notes are built even for an explicit --list, so the whole-tree gate pays a second front end per file that has a #if again

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-CLI-UNROUTED
arms.note: the CLI no longer answers to `add-meta`, so the dispatch, argument parsing and --write half of the op has no test reaching it

arms.name: M-LINT-RANGE-INERT
arms.replace:
if (range == null) return all;
if (all != null) return all;
arms.note: the --range window stops filtering, so a write op's --fix rewrites every finding in the file instead of only those on the lines it changed

arms.name: M-LINTFIX-ACCEPTED-BLAMED
arms.find:
case Ok(text, rewrites):
settled = { text: text, rewrites: rewrites };
arms.note: a file whose whole edit set the gate accepted is still counted as refused, so the run summary blames a rule nothing declined

arms.name: M-EXIT-STATUS-AGREES
arms.note: a transcript is never reconciled against the exit status its runner returned, so a shard killed mid-run summarises green again and its partial counts enter the aggregate as if the missing tests had passed

arms.name: M-MOVE-CANONICALISE-ALWAYS
arms.find: return CanonicalEdit.isWriterCanonical(original, plugin, opts) ? fixedPointChange(cmd, change, plugin, opts) : change;
arms.note: a move canonicalises every file it writes, so a source that was already non-canonical on disk is reformatted by an edit that asked only for a splice

arms.name: M-SOURCE-READ-GUARD-OFF
arms.note: `apq source <file>` with nothing narrowing the read prints the whole file again at exit 0 — the cat behaviour that cost 617 585 bytes over this tree's three largest files

arms.name: M-PROBE-SLOT-CONST
arms.note: every process stages to one machine-global path again, so a second worker's source answers the first one's `strip` / `recon --probe` with exit 0 and no exception

arms.name: M-PROBE-STAGE-ANY-TARGET
arms.note: staging writes whatever the slot names, so a planted symlink there is a write-anywhere primitive with this process's rights

arms.name: M-TEST-SUMMARY-GLOBAL-DEFAULT
arms.note: a source-less run reaches for one machine-global transcript again, so a second worker's suite log answers the first worker's counts at exit 0

arms.name: M-STDLIB-DUP-WORKDIR-SHARED
arms.replace: final base: String = requested ?? haxe.io.Path.join([TempScratch.root(), WORK_DIR_STEM]);
arms.note: every run stages its generated probe into one machine-global directory under one fixed module name again, so two concurrent runs compile each other's program and report a fully-formed finding about the wrong function

arms.name: M-STDLIB-DUP-WORK-ANY-TARGET
arms.note: the work directory is whatever the slot names, so a symlink planted there is adopted: the generated probe is written through it and every non-directory entry of the victim is deleted when the run ends

arms.name: M-LEDGER-CROSS-FILE-MUTE
arms.note: the cross-file clause attaches to the rules that do NOT carry the seam, so the one rule whose edits only land there is reported as saying nothing again

arms.name: M-SCOPE-GAP-UNWIRED
arms.note: the missing-roots notice is written but never called, which is what moving it below the --fix early return would also do - the message fixtures stay green and every run goes silent

arms.name: M-SCOPE-GAP-ROOT-UNWIRED
arms.note: a declared resolutionRoots entry that matches no .hx goes back to being read, dropped and never mentioned - the only place that learns it stops saying so

arms.name: M-LIT-SYNTHETIC-KINDS-EMPTY
arms.note: `apq lit` stops declaring the two kinds it mints itself, so the gate - which reads the grammar and nothing else - refuses the documented `--kind Comment` / `--kind Directive` as typos and every comment or directive hunt becomes a usage error

arms.name: M-AST-SELECT-UNKNOWN-KIND-EXIT-OK
arms.note: `apq ast --select` on a kind no grammar projects goes back to exit 0, so the message says typo and the status says answer - and a script driving ast cannot tell a misspelling from a file that simply holds none

arms.name: M-AST-SELECT-NO-CROSS-PROJECT-HINT
arms.find: final crossProjectHint: String = firstKind.length > 0 && firstKind.fastCodeAt(0) >= 'A'.code && firstKind.fastCodeAt(0) <= 'Z'.code
arms.replace: final crossProjectHint: String = firstKind.length < 0 && firstKind.fastCodeAt(0) >= 'A'.code && firstKind.fastCodeAt(0) <= 'Z'.code
arms.note: a `--select` miss on a TypeName loses the pointer at the multi-file walkers, so the reader of a single-file miss is told the kind is wrong and never that `refs` / `uses` / `blast` are where the declaration would be found

arms.name: M-ORACLE-EXCLUSIONS-UNNAMED
arms.note: the driver stops naming excluded configurations, so a net or phase shrunk to the green subset reads as covering every build

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-ORACLE-DROPS-DEFINES
arms.note: the display server is warmed and queried without its configuration's defines, so it names types for a build nobody judges

arms.name: M-ORACLE-EXCLUSIONS-KEYED-BY-SENTENCE
arms.note: exclusions are deduped by sentence, so a red build whose error line moved after a safe fix is named twice with two reasons

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RACED-VERIFIES-FIXES
arms.note: a generation that raced an input still verifies --fix, so a build that does not match the tree can veto a sound fix

arms.name: M-ORACLE-SUMMARY-SILENT
arms.note: apq oracle ends without counting the unavailable configurations, so its exit 0 reads as every configuration confirmed

arms.name: M-FIAD-ROOTS-MATCH-IGNORED
arms.note: a declared `resolutionRoots` entry matching no `.hx` counts as a working root, so the crossing path admits an init over a scope that is the report alone

arms.name: M-REACH-CONFIGS-COMPLETE
arms.note: the oracle list is read as every build the project ships, so a platform branch no configuration compiles is skipped

arms.name: M-REACH-CONFIGS-AGREE
arms.note: the first path's config decides the flag for the run, so a path whose own config ships other builds is judged under the first's

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-NOT-ATTACHED
arms.find: return OracleRunMemo.attach(prepared.oracles, new OracleRunMemo(persisted, () -> [for (f in files) f.file]));
arms.note: a lint run's configurations carry no memo, so every phase compiles the tree it asks about again

arms.name: M-FACTS-NEVER-EARLY
arms.note: no run starts its facts compiles ahead, so they follow the first check that asks instead of overlapping the checks

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-FACTS-FIRST
arms.note: the oracle-assisted phase asks the display server although the run holds every configuration's facts

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-DECLINE-CENSUS
arms.note: the oracle-assisted phase prints no decline reason

arms.name: M-FIX-FACTS-SETTLED
arms.find:
// no disk write before this one but a create, which settled the facts compiles already
		cached.compilerFactsSettled();
arms.note: the safe pass writes while the early facts compiles may still be reading the files

arms.name: M-LINT-SUMMARY-NEVER
arms.note: a text report over its threshold, or asked for --summary, still lists every finding

arms.name: M-REFLECTIVE-BUILDS
arms.find: if (builds != null && reflective != null) builds.reflectiveClasses = reflective;
arms.note: the declared `reflectiveClasses` never reach the builds the reach analysis reads

arms.name: M-REFLECTIVE-WARN
arms.note: a declared glob matching no class the builds typed goes unreported

arms.name: M-REFLECTIVE-AGREE
arms.note: the first path's declaration bounds the run, so a path declaring other classes, or none, is judged under the first's

arms.name: M-HOLDERS-BUILDS
arms.find: if (builds != null && holders != null) builds.reflectiveMethodHolders = holders;
arms.note: the declared `reflectiveMethodHolders` never reach the builds the reach analysis reads

arms.name: M-HOLDERS-WARN
arms.note: a declared method-holder glob matching no class the builds typed goes unreported

arms.name: M-HOLDERS-READ
arms.note: the run never reads the declared `reflectiveMethodHolders`

arms.name: M-LINTFIX-FINDING-SPLIT-NONE
arms.find: final pieces: Array<RuleEdits> = split == null || group.findings.length < 2 ? [] : split(group);
arms.note: a refused edit set is never re-asked a finding at a time, so one refused finding costs its rule every other finding in the file

arms.name: M-LINTFIX-GUARD-SPLIT-NONE
arms.note: a guard refusal drops the check's whole edit set again, so the finding the guard names costs its clean siblings their fix

arms.name: M-LINTFIX-BLAME-SITE-ALWAYS
arms.note: a whole group's blame line names a site too, so the bare rule id the reader keys on changes shape whenever the group holds one finding

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-SALVAGE-NONE
arms.find: if (settled == null || settled.text == source) return null;
arms.replace: if (settled == null || settled.text == source || true) return null;
arms.note: a refused oracle-assisted edit set keeps nothing, so one un-writable annotation costs the file every other

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-SPLIT-NONE
arms.find: source, groups, why, plugin, optsJson, blamed, split
arms.replace: source, groups, why, plugin, optsJson, blamed
arms.note: a refused assisted rule is never re-asked a finding at a time, so one refused finding costs the rule its others in the file

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-SALVAGED-COUNT-ALL
arms.find: for (group in groups) if (group.refusal == null && !group.overlapped) edits += group.edits.length;
arms.note: a salvaged file reports the edits it was asked for, the refused ones included, as applied

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-REFUSAL-SILENT
arms.note: an assisted refusal is dropped without a line or a summary count again

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-REFUSAL-LEDGER-NONE
arms.note: an assisted refusal reaches no ledger row, so the gate-refusal block never names the rule

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-FMT-GATE-OFF
arms.find: final stranded: Null<String> = isCanonical ? null : OrphanContinuation.introduced(source, formatted, plugin);
arms.note: fmt writes whatever the writer emits, so a writer defect that strands an else rewrites the file to code the compiler rejects

arms.name: M-AHEAD-NEVER-READ
arms.find: final found: Null<ReachBuilds> = pending == null ? ReachDefinesProbe.probeAll(oracles) : ReachDefinesProbe.finish(pending);
arms.note: the compiles started ahead are never read, so every run that escalates pays the builds twice

arms.name: M-AHEAD-READ-AFTER-WRITE
arms.note: the compiles started ahead answer a question asked after the run wrote, so the builds describe a tree that is gone

arms.name: M-BUILDS-WITH-FACTS
arms.note: the builds' probe compiles wait for the first reach question, which then waits on them alone half-way through the first pass

arms.name: M-SAFE-NET-PLAIN
arms.note: the safe-write net compiles the written tree plainly, so the risky phase's coverage probe compiles every configuration of it again with -v

arms.name: M-SCORE-LOST-EXIT
arms.note: a lost real stall no longer fails the scoring run

arms.name: M-LINT-NOFILE-DROPPED
arms.note: a finding naming no file only counts in the summary line

arms.name: M-LINT-EXPLAIN-UNSET
arms.note: `--explain-long` never asks the check to explain, so the run prints no evidence

arms.name: M-LINT-EXPLAIN-NO-ENVELOPE
arms.note: --explain-long --format json prints the bare array when thread-safety is not in the run, so a consumer cannot tell asked from not asked

arms.name: M-REMOVE-ELEMENT-KIND-IGNORED
arms.note: remove-element ignores --kind and re-reads the address by its first token, so a match that starts no statement removes the call ARGUMENT instead of the statement the kind names

arms.name: M-RISKYARM-NOT-VERIFIED
arms.note: a RiskyArm check never reaches the verifier, so its arm is report-only even with an oracle

arms.name: M-SAFE-REVERT-ABORTS
arms.find: fixedCount -= settleRevert(safePass, safeEditsOf, changedFiles, files, originalOf, true);
arms.note: the run stops after a safe revert, before the risky and oracle-assisted phases, although the revert left the tree green

arms.name: M-SAFE-REVERT-EDITS-COUNTED
arms.note: the summary still counts the edits of the files the net rolled back

arms.name: M-SAFE-REVERT-FILES-COUNTED
arms.note: the summary still counts a reverted file as changed

arms.name: M-SAFE-REVERT-EXIT-OK
arms.note: a run that had to revert a safe fix exits as a success

arms.name: M-SAFE-REVERT-UNSAID
arms.note: the run goes on after a safe revert without saying so

arms.name: M-FIXDRIVER-SUPERSEDES-IGNORED
arms.note: the fixer counts an underscore-prefixed binding twice - once from the active scope, once from the full one

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-REPORTED-TWICE
arms.note: a RiskyArm rule's arm findings reach `reported` a second time (the safe loop counted them), so the row reads 5 of 7 for five findings

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-HANDOFF-KEPT
arms.note: the safe arm's hand-off declines stay beside the arm's own verdict, so each arm finding is declined twice, or declined although the arm fixed it

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-HANDOFF-UNRECORDED
arms.note: no hand-off is recorded, so the risky phase has nothing to take back and the arm findings are declined twice

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-ARM-BLIND
arms.note: the safe loop does not ask the RiskyArm which findings its arm owns, so no hand-off is ever recorded

arms.name: M-LEDGER-ARM-LISTED-ABSENT
arms.note: a RiskyArm rule is footnoted as absent from the ledger (and counted never asked) beside its own row

arms.name: M-HELPER-DRY-RUN-WRITES
arms.note: a dry run writes the files it was only asked to print

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-CONSTANT-ADDRESSED-UNROUTED
arms.note: the addressed flags reach the literal modes, which reject them

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-DRY-RUN-UNROUTED
arms.note: --dry-run prints the two previews instead of the entries and their digest

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-CONSTANT-INTO-SCAN-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: the module reached through a symlinked scope is scanned as a consumer of itself, so its sites and the module are written from one stale source

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-CONSTANT-TO-INTO-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: --into naming the source through a symlink counts as another module, so --to refuses the source's own type

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-INTO-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: --into naming the source through a symlink counts as a second module, so one file is staged twice and the write half-lands

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-CLI-BLIND-SEAT
arms.note: the op reads the file with no project resolution scope, so the insert seat takes every wildcard for a run boundary and places the import where the import-order rule does not

arms.name: M-REMOVEIMPORT-CLI-USING-FLAG-DROPPED
arms.note: remove-import --using parses and then drops the flag, so the bare path beside an import of the same module is ambiguous again

arms.name: M-MENTIONS-IMPORT-KINDS-UNPASSED
arms.find: Lit.find(target, entry.tree, true, null, delimiters, ModuleScan.IMPORT_DECL_KINDS)
arms.note: mentions <Name> answers the uses and not the dotted `import pkg.Name;` that makes them resolve, and the reader concludes there is no import

arms.name: M-FIX-REMOVE-IGNORED
arms.note: a slice that removes a file is staged and never committed, so a fix that deletes a file reports success and leaves it on disk

arms.name: M-FIX-REMOVE-NO-RESTORE
arms.find: if (original == null || files.exists(entry -> entry.file == path)) continue;
arms.note: the safe-pass revert restores the files the run still holds only, so a deletion the oracle rejected stays deleted and the tree the revert claims green does not compile

arms.name: M-FIX-AMBIENT-HELD
arms.note: an ambient source a pass rewrote stays in memory until the end of the run, so every later pass resolves the chain from the statements the source no longer carries

arms.name: M-FIX-OVERLAP-BLIND
arms.note: the edits two cross-file fixes make in one file are merged unchecked, so where they overlap the later silently swallows the earlier and the run reports both as landed

arms.name: M-REACH-STORED-UNREAD
arms.find: if (noOracle) return withStoredBuilds(resolution, oracles, reflective, holders);
arms.note: a run that compiles nothing never reads the builds an oracle run stored, so it knows no build and the alias branch no build takes is read again

arms.name: M-HOIST-MIXED-LISTS-GUESSED
arms.note: a run over paths whose configs name different oracle lists, one of them declared complete, carries no hold, so hoist-common-import falls back on classpath evidence and `--fix` writes an ambient statement a build of the declared list cannot resolve

arms.name: M-HELD-NOTE-LOST-WITH-FACTS
arms.note: the scope an oracle run hands its checks drops the hold, so a run whose declared builds did not answer falls back on classpath evidence and says nothing

arms.name: M-CATEGORY-FILTER-IGNORED
arms.note: --category is parsed and validated but narrows nothing, so a run reports every category

arms.name: M-CATEGORY-FORCES-RULES
arms.note: --category bypasses the config the way --rule does, so a rule the config disables runs under its category

arms.name: M-SAFE-BAN-OFF
arms.note: an edit the safe-pass net took back is offered again by the follow-up round, which re-applies it and reverts it a second time

arms.name: M-SAFE-PLACE-SKIPPED
arms.note: a culprit the net reverts whole is left on disk at the last candidate an isolation probe wrote, while the run reports the tree back to a green build

arms.name: M-LINT-STD-IN-DECLARED
arms.note: the declared half of the scope carries the std too, so a scan of the project's own code reads the std

arms.name: M-SAFE-PROBE-WRITE-ESCAPES
arms.note: a candidate the disk refuses escapes the isolation as a WriteFailure, so the settle never runs and the disk stays on a candidate the oracle may have rejected

arms.name: M-SAFE-DELETE-REFUSAL-IGNORED
arms.find: if (!CliIo.deletePath(file)) throw new WriteFailure(file, 'the file could not be deleted');
arms.note: a file the filesystem refuses to delete is taken as gone, so a probe compiles a candidate that still holds it

arms.name: M-SAFE-SETTLE-RAW-EXCEPTION
arms.replace: throw new Exception('cannot write ' + wrong.join(', ') + ': ' + reason);
arms.note: a settled tree the disk does not hold stops the run with a bare exception: a raw stack, no summary line, not EXIT_RUNTIME

arms.name: M-FOREIGN-RULE-ANSWERED
arms.note: an explicit --rule naming a rule the run's grammar never runs is answered with an empty report, which reads as a clean file

arms.name: M-FOREIGN-RULE-ALWAYS
arms.note: a default or --category lint over a grammar some builtin is not bound to is refused, so every apq lint --lang json|mermaid exits 2

arms.name: M-SCOPED-LISTING-UNFILTERED
arms.note: the scoped --list-rules lists a rule the scope's grammar never runs as a state of that scope's lint

arms.name: M-GRAPH-DIFF-MODULE-FUNCTION-UNNAMED
arms.note: a module-level function is named without the module type the call graph places it in, so a change to its text is never seen

arms.name: M-GRAPH-DIFF-RENAME-UNPAIRED
arms.note: a file renamed between the revisions is paired by path, finds no earlier text, and every edit inside it goes unseen

arms.name: M-FLOW-CLI-NOT-WIRED
arms.find: return flow == null ? drawScope(request, ctx) : GraphFlow.run(COMMAND, flow, request.inputSpecs, request.lang, request.output, ctx);
arms.note: graph --flow draws the graph of the whole scope instead of the chart of the function named
